um-ma-nu i!?/ad#/ṣi#/DUMU# [...]
#note: Already von Soden (@bib{RN2198a@164}) and Foster (@bib{RN164@412}) considered NinNA5 the beginning of the text. Parpola (@bib{RN310@450}), who considered Counsels of Wisdom as “the Babylonian archetype of the Sayings of Ahiqar” and aimed to identify Aba-ninnu-dari/Ahiqar as its author, restored here @akk{um-ma-nu DUMU!-[šu₂ i-mal-lik]}. Collation by Oshima allegedly confirms the reading @akk{DUM[U]} (see @bib{RN3102a@61 n. 11}); the clear @akk{i}- on Lambert’s autograph and a comparison with @akk{TUR} in l. 7 call for caution. The opening lines resemble the introduction of Examenstext A (@bib{fromebllab0020@193-194}).
